newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Guangdong Tannery seen strong on debut.
newsitem.headline: Guangdong Tannery seen strong on debut.

text.p: Prospects of a pick-up in Chinese consumer spending should boost Guangdong Tannery shares on Monday when the unit of Guangdong Investment Ltd begins trading in Hong Kong, analysts said on Thursday.
Guangdong Tannery processes cow hides and sheep skins to make semi-finished and finished leather products.

"Investors who want to tap the growing consumer market in China will find the stock an attractive buy because the shares are not that expensive," said Sunny Chan, research manager at Seapower Research.
Analysts said a high grey market price, following a strong subscription response, and a continuous demand for quality China-related stocks would also boost demand for the shares.
The grey market price was about HK$2.50 per share compared with an issue price of HK$1.03 per share, they said.

Guangdong Tannery offered 110 million new shares in an offering in Hong Kong, of which 71 million were offered on a preferential basis to Guangdong Investment shareholders of one Guangdong Tannery share for every 20 Guangdong Investment shares held.
Thirty million shares were offered for public subscription and were 667 times subscribed, the highest subscription level for a Hong Kong initial public offering this year.
"It is not surprising that the shares had such a strong subscription level because only a small amount of shares was available for public subscription," said Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment.
"I expect strong demand for the shares and the limited supply of shares will give the shares a boost on their debut," Ng added.
The company had said it was able to net interest income of HK$14 million on the subscription funds.
The company said the net proceeds of the issue would be used to expand and upgrade production facilities in China.
Guangdong Investment will hold 75 percent of Guangdong Tannery after the issue and listing.
